---
name: read-tree-commit-race
description: A fresh index plus read-tree HEAD still clobbers — commit writes the whole index, so any path another lane advances between snapshot and commit is reverted
metadata:

The fresh-index discipline (rm -f index; `read-tree HEAD`; add explicit paths; confirm the
staged stat lists only those paths; commit) is necessary and NOT sufficient. `read-tree
HEAD` snapshots the whole tree into the index; `commit` writes the whole index as a tree —
not just the paths you added. So every path in the repo is silently staged at its
read-tree-time revision, and any that another lane advances in the interval gets reverted
by your commit.

**Why:** it produces an `M` against a stale blob, not a `D`, so grepping `^D` finds
nothing. The pre-commit `diff --cached --name-status HEAD` is CORRECT at the time it runs —
HEAD had not moved yet. Per-file `lake env lean`, hash-vs-disk on your own paths, sorry
census and axiom probe all pass, because the files are fine and the damage is to somebody
else's path.

**How to apply:** the only check that catches it is AFTER committing —
`git ... diff HEAD~1 HEAD --stat` (or `show HEAD --stat --format=`) and read every path. A
path you did not add means you reverted it; restore from disk, which still holds their
version. Keep rm-f/read-tree/add/commit as one uninterrupted sequence to shrink the window,
but the audit-after is the reliable half. Filed as I-1271; ajc-p2 independently hit the same
